name: Banu Qasi
alt: Banu Qasi lords of the Ebro

predecessors.name: Emirate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: Zaragoza and Tudela, entered by the sons of Musa ibn Musa in 872

successors.name: Kingdom of Pamplona
successors.text: Nájera and Viguera in La Rioja

ledger.x: 872: the sons of Musa ibn Musa take Zaragoza and Tudela.
By 884 Monzón is no longer Banu Qasi land: the page has Muhammad ibn Lubb 'regain' Monzón and Lleida in 914, so it was lost, but it does not say when or to whom.
898: the Banu Qasi hold Tudela and Tarazona as the emir's vassals.
898: Lubb ibn Muhammad is given Tarazona, with Tudela already his.
914: Muhammad ibn Lubb regains Monzón and Lleida.
914: the Rioja lands around Nájera and Viguera are in Banu Qasi hands.
924: Abd al-Rahman III ends the vassalage by removing the Banu Qasi from Tudela: 'on his return to Tudela he removed the Banu Qasi and sent them to Córdoba'.

924: Abd al-Rahman III removes the Banu Qasi from Tudela. the Banu Qasi page: 'on his return to Tudela he removed the Banu Qasi and sent them to Córdoba', the year after 'Viguera and Najera fell' (923); the Tujibids take their place.
929: the Banu Qasi end in the Ebro valley.

wars.name: Banu Qasi revolts against Córdoba
wars.outcome: Musa ibn Musa revolts with Íñigo Arista in the 840s and is defeated by Abd ar-Rahman II (his son Lubb taken hostage); after the 870 Huesca rebellion the family returns to dominance (872), Mutarrif and his sons are crucified at Córdoba in 873 and the emir…

wars.name: Wars of Sancho Garcés I and Abd al-Rahman III against the Banu Qasi
wars.outcome: Lubb is killed at Liédena (30 September 907); Sancho takes Arnedo (914) and captures Abd Allah at Tudela (915); Ordoño II and Sancho ravage Viguera, Nájera and Tudela (918); Viguera and Nájera fall (923); the emir removes them from Tudela (924); Muhammad ibn…

certainty.note: Held towns and fortresses along the Ebro; the page gives no boundary lines.
